about: Roper Technologies is a diversified technology company based in Sarasota, Florida, listed on Nasdaq (ROP). It owns and acquires niche software and technology businesses, including Deltek, Aderant, Procare and Neptune, selling to government, legal, education, healthcare and utility customers, with revenue of about $7.5 billion. It moved from industrial products to being mainly software over the past decade. Strictly B2B with little consumer brand awareness.

Rawabi Holding is a Saudi Arabian diversified group based in Al Khobar, with businesses in oil and gas services, petrochemicals, construction, consumer goods, real estate and healthcare, partnering with international firms such as Vitol (Rawabi Vitol) and Hanwha. Customers are energy companies, government and consumers. Privately held, founded in 1975. Crunchbase shows funding of about SAR 7.2 billion. Strong regional brand within Saudi business, mostly B2B.

about: Nanya Technology is a Taiwanese maker of DRAM memory chips, part of the Formosa Plastics Group, founded in 1995 and listed in Taipei (2408). It supplies standard, specialty and mobile DRAM to makers of PCs, servers, consumer electronics, networking and automotive equipment, operating fabs in New Taipei, Taiwan. Revenue comes from chip sales to electronics manufacturers worldwide. B2B component supplier with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

SJ Semi (SJSemi) is a Chinese semiconductor packaging and foundry-services company based in Jiangyin, Jiangsu, and part of the JCET Group ecosystem, focused on middle-end-of-line wafer processing such as bumping, redistribution layers and wafer-level packaging for advanced chips. Customers are chip designers and foundries. B2B manufacturer with no consumer brand awareness. Established in the 2010s as a Chinese integrated circuit packaging supplier.

about: Polaris Inc. is a manufacturer of off-road vehicles, snowmobiles, motorcycles and boats, with brands including Polaris RZR and Ranger, Indian Motorcycle, Slingshot, Ski-Doo competitors, Pontoon boats and Aixam. It sells through dealers worldwide to consumers and commercial customers, with revenue of about 7 billion dollars and 15,000 employees. Founded in 1954 in Roseau, Minnesota, and headquartered in Medina (Long Lake area), Minnesota. Listed on the NYSE (PII). Strong enthusiast consumer brand with extensive racing and event sponsorship experience.

wiki.title: Polaris
wiki.what: Northern pole-star; brightest star in Ursa Minor
wiki.text: Polaris is a yellow supergiant star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Ursa Minor. It is designated α Ursae Minoris and is commonly called the North Star. With an apparent magnitude that fluctuates around 1.98, it is the brightest star in the constellation and is readily visible to the naked eye at night. The position of the star lies less than 1° away from the north celestial pole, making it the current northern pole star. The stable position of the star in the Northern Sky makes it useful for navigation.

wiki.title: Polaris Inc.
wiki.text: Polaris Inc. is an American automotive manufacturer headquartered in Medina, Minnesota, United States. Polaris was founded in Roseau, Minnesota, where it still has engineering and manufacturing facilities. The company manufactured motorcycles through its Victory Motorcycles subsidiary until January 2017, then produced motorcycles through the Indian Motorcycle subsidiary, which it purchased in April 2011 and announced its divestiture in October 2025. Polaris produced personal watercraft from 1994 to 2004. The company was originally named Polaris Industries Inc. and was renamed in 2019 to Polaris Inc.

about: EuroGroup Laminations is an industrial maker of laminations for electric motors, generators and transformers, using electrical steel. It is Italian in origin, with plants in Europe, the US, Mexico and China, though this record lists a Paris, Tennessee address. Customers are motor and EV component manufacturers. Funding of about 515 million is shown. B2B component supplier with no consumer brand awareness. Current ownership and listing status were not confirmed.

about: HAI Robotics is a Shenzhen-based warehouse automation company that makes autonomous case-handling robots (ACR) and the HaiPick systems, which lift totes and cartons in warehouses for e-commerce, retail, manufacturing and apparel. Founded in 2016, it has deployed systems across dozens of countries, backed by Tencent and Hillhouse. Revenue is from robot systems and software. B2B robotics brand with no consumer awareness.

Klockner Pentaplast is a global manufacturer of rigid and flexible plastic films and packaging for pharmaceutical, food and medical markets, with plants in about 18 countries. Headquartered in Montabaur, Germany, though Crunchbase shows London, it went through a financial restructuring in 2024 that put control with its lenders. Customers are drugmakers and food producers. B2B packaging supplier with no consumer brand awareness. Funding of about 564 million is shown.

about: Parkland is a Calgary, Alberta fuel distributor and convenience store operator, listed on the TSX (PKI), with retail brands including Chevron, Ultramar, Pioneer and On the Run in Canada, plus fuel supply operations in the US and the Caribbean and the Burnaby refinery. It serves consumers, commercial fleets and industrial customers. Revenue is about 30 billion Canadian dollars. In 2025 it agreed to be acquired by Sunoco LP. Its retail fuel stations have high consumer visibility across Canada.

SK Siltron CSS is the silicon carbide (SiC) wafer business of South Korea's SK Siltron, based in Bay City, Michigan, which it acquired from DuPont in 2020. It makes SiC substrates and epitaxial wafers used in electric vehicle power electronics, chargers and renewable energy inverters, supported by a US government CHIPS Act grant and Department of Energy loan. Customers are power chip manufacturers. Part of the SK Group. B2B semiconductor materials supplier with no consumer awareness.

Meitu is a Xiamen, China-based consumer app company, founded in 2008 and listed in Hong Kong (HKEX: 1357), best known for the Meitu Xiu Xiu and BeautyCam photo-editing apps, and the Wink video editor and Meitu Design Studio. It earns subscription revenue from hundreds of millions of monthly users, plus advertising and cross-border sales of former Meitu smartphones, and holds large crypto and digital asset reserves. Strong consumer app brand in China and parts of Asia.

Panavision is a Woodland Hills, California-based designer and manufacturer of high-precision camera lenses and cameras for film and television, and a major equipment rental business, now owned by Ranger Global. Panavision cameras have been used on many Hollywood movies. Customers are studios and cinematographers. Highly recognised in the film industry; limited consumer awareness.

Meshy AI is a Sunnyvale, California-based AI platform that turns text and images into 3D models, textures and animations for game developers, designers, 3D printing and virtual worlds. It claims millions of users. The Crunchbase funding figure of about $450 million looks inconsistent with reported rounds, so treat it with caution. Creative software with rising online awareness in developer circles.

about: Velo3D is a Fremont, California-based metal 3D printing company, selling Sapphire laser powder bed fusion printers and software for aerospace, defence and energy parts. Listed via a SPAC in 2021, then delisted and later relisted on Nasdaq after restructuring; Arrayed Notes is its main shareholder. Customers include SpaceX and other aerospace names. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

Unitree Robotics is a Hangzhou-based Chinese robotics company, making quadruped robot dogs (Go2, B2) and humanoid robots (H1, G1) for research, entertainment and industrial uses, with a strong rise in profile in 2025. The input location is garbled. It has been preparing a STAR Market IPO. Known in tech circles and online for viral robot videos.

wiki.title: Unitree Robotics
wiki.text: Hangzhou Yushu Technology Co., Ltd., doing business as Unitree Robotics, is a robotics company based in Hangzhou, China. Founded by Wang Xingxing in August 2016, Unitree initially specialized in quadruped robots for the consumer market. In 2024, the company began producing humanoid robots, with the second iteration priced around US$16,000.

about: Kingboard is a Hong Kong investment holding group, based in Sha Tin, whose companies make copper-clad laminates, printed circuit boards, chemicals and property investments. Kingboard Holdings (HKEX: 148) and Kingboard Laminates are among the world's largest laminate makers, selling to electronics manufacturers. Revenue is tens of billions of Hong Kong dollars. B2B with no consumer brand.

IMA Group is an Italian maker of automatic machines for packaging pharmaceuticals, tea, coffee, and cosmetics, based in Castenaso, near Bologna. Customers are pharmaceutical, food and beverage companies worldwide, and revenue is around 2 billion euros. Founded in 1961, it is controlled by Alberto Vacchi and BC Partners, which bought a major stake in 2020. B2B and in the Emilia-Romagna 'Packaging Valley' cluster, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Inverse Multiplexing for ATM
wiki.text: Inverse Multiplexing for ATM (IMA) is a standardized technology used to transport ATM traffic over a bundle of T1 or E1 lines, which is called an IMA Group. This allows for gradual increase in data link capacity where implementing a higher capacity solution like T3/E3 or SONET/SDH is not deemed feasible. The maximum number of lines in an IMA Group is 32, bringing the total data rate to roughly 64 Mbit/s. The standard specification was initially approved by The ATM Forum in July 1997, and was later updated to version 1.1 in March 1999.

about: Atomic Machines is an Emeryville, California deep-tech company developing atomic-scale manufacturing technology for MEMS, semiconductors and nano devices, with ambitions to build precise structures atom by atom. Recorded funding is about 250 million dollars, though this figure looks high for a startup at its stage. Customers would be chipmakers and advanced manufacturers. Privately held. Early-stage technology brand with no consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Axalta Coating Systems is a global coatings maker headquartered in Philadelphia, producing liquid and powder coatings for car refinish (Cromax, Standox, Spies Hecker brands), light vehicles, commercial vehicles and industrial applications. It was carved out of DuPont's performance coatings business in 2013, after Carlyle bought it. Customers are body shops, car makers and industrial manufacturers, and it has revenue of around $5 billion with roughly 12,000 employees and sales in about 130 countries. It is listed on the NYSE (AXTA). B2B brand with a long record in motorsport sponsorship, including NASCAR.

wiki.title: Axalta
wiki.text: Axalta Coating Systems Ltd., also known as simply Axalta, is an American company specializing in coatings in a wide variety of industrial applications, materials and sectors, including automotive paints. The company is based in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and incorporated in Bermuda. Axalta develops and manufactures coatings for light and commercial vehicles, industrial, and refinish applications. The firm does business in 130 countries, has nearly 13,000 employees, and has more than 100,000 customers.

about: AssetWatch is a Dublin, Ohio, condition monitoring company that sells wireless sensors and analytics for industrial machinery, alerting plant maintenance teams about faults such as bearing wear. Customers are manufacturers and process plants, paying monthly subscriptions. Founded in 2018, it raised about $166 million, including a 2025 round. B2B industrial IoT brand with no consumer awareness. Its subscription revenue is recurring, and it sells to plant managers and reliability engineers, so there is no consumer awareness and sponsorship relevance is limited.

Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment (AMEC) is a Shanghai-based Chinese semiconductor equipment maker, producing plasma etching machines and MOCVD equipment used by chip and LED manufacturers. Customers are leading chip fabs in China and abroad, and it earns revenue from equipment sales and servicing. Founded in 2004, it is listed on Shanghai's STAR Market (688012). Crunchbase shows about $159 million of funding. B2B industrial technology brand with no consumer awareness.

ARRIS, now Arris Composites, is a US advanced manufacturing company based in Berkeley, California, that developed additive moulding, a process for making complex continuous-fibre composite parts by moulding compressed fibre bundles. It makes lightweight carbon-fibre components for aerospace, automotive, medical and consumer products, selling parts and licences to manufacturers. It is venture backed and has raised about 239 million dollars. B2B materials technology brand with little public awareness.

wiki.title: Arris International
wiki.text: Arris International Limited was an American telecommunications equipment company engaged in data, video and telephony systems for homes and businesses.

about: Fictiv is a San Francisco digital manufacturing platform that lets engineers and product teams order custom parts, such as CNC-machined, injection-moulded and 3D-printed components, through an online quote system with a network of vetted factories in the US and Asia. Customers are hardware and robotics companies, automotive, aerospace and medical device firms, paying per order, with software for project management. Founded in 2013 by Dave Evans, it raised about 190 million dollars and was acquired in 2025 by Japanese industrial supplier MISUMI Group. B2B engineering brand with strong recognition among product engineers, none among consumers.

about: US-based global courier and logistics company running FedEx Express, Ground and Freight services, along with supply chain, e-commerce and customs solutions, delivering packages to over 220 countries with revenue near 88 billion dollars and 500,000 employees. Customers are consumers, shippers and enterprises. Headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee; founded 1971 by Fred Smith. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (FDX), with a freight spin-off planned for 2026. Very strong B2B and consumer brand, with extensive sponsorship history including NASCAR, NFL and Formula 1.

wiki.title: FedEx
wiki.text: FedEx Corporation is an American multinational transportation, e-commerce, and business-services company headquartered in Memphis, Tennessee. Founded in 1971 by Frederick W. Smith as Federal Express Corporation, it began operations in 1973 as an express delivery company centered on an air-and-ground network based at Memphis International Airport. FedEx now provides parcel delivery, express transportation, freight forwarding, logistics, customs brokerage, supply-chain services, and retail printing and shipping services worldwide. In fiscal 2026, the company reported revenue of $94.7 billion and employed about 452,000 people.

about: Gopuff is a US instant delivery service for snacks, groceries, alcohol, personal care and household items from micro-fulfilment centres, with 15-minute-style delivery in many cities and a retail presence through BevMo, which it owns. Customers are consumers using the Gopuff app, and it has operated in the US and the UK and Ireland. Headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; founded 2013. Privately held with SoftBank and others as investors, valued at about 15 billion dollars in 2021. Known to US urban consumers, with a history of sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Gopuff
wiki.text: GoBrands, Inc., doing business as Gopuff, is an American consumer goods and food delivery company headquartered in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The company delivers foods and goods typically found in convenience stores in more than 500 cities, suburbs, and towns across the United States as of 2025. It also operates in the United Kingdom, following an acquisition of Newcastle upon Tyne-based Fancy.

about: PODS is a Clearwater, Florida portable moving and storage company that delivers storage containers to homes and businesses, then picks them up and moves or stores them, operating in the US, Canada and Australia. Founded in 1998, it earns from container rentals, moves and storage, and uses franchise and licensee partners. Owned by Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan since 2021. Private. Recognisable consumer-facing brand in North America with mass-market advertising.
